assign.outcome:
**Zero container queries in `ext/Panel` — `hug` measures what it holds, and a document measures all the way down.**

![](hug-auto.png)

- **61 cq lines to 0 live** (CSSOM-verified: no `container-type`, no `@container`, no cq unit anywhere in the module). 10 mentions survive as comments saying what went. panel 10 · size 2 · templates 39 · toolbar 6 · tools 4 → 0.
- **`hug` = auto.** One line 52px · twelve lines 656px · a scene at its own floor. Was 16em for all three.
- **The scrollbar rule holds.** Same document, same seeds: three rolled sections went 241/241/241 with **55 boxes scrolling their own content** → 13012/1832/5062 with **0**. A plain document of bands: 3 → 0. The 55 leaf widths are identical to the pixel — nothing touched the inline axis.
- **One roll = one section.** `workspace.js`'s `sown()`, one `item.document()` test.
- **Nothing else moved.** Four pages at 1280, ten workspaces, identical panel counts and identical box sizes before/after (measured by swapping the files back), zero console errors. The cells demo still shows three 83.17px tracks.

**Two rules the design said would not be needed** — both the same fact, that a `flex: 1 1 0` child contributes zero to a box measuring itself: `.panel.panel-h-hug > :is(.panel-body, .panel-items) { flex-basis: auto }` (a cross-axis hug read **0px**), and the last rule in `panel.css` (nothing in a document divides the block axis). [decisions](/framework/ext/Panel/doc/decisions.md).

**Also:** `--panel-hug` → `--panel-section` (the document floor, not a width) · `.hug` deleted, `size.css` says it per axis · `.panel-t-scene` is the new class a drawing with nothing to measure wears · `.panel-workspace`/`.panel-items` now state `position: relative`, which `container-type: size` was doing by accident · the bar folds unconditionally · `wall` is two columns.

**Left, named:** furniture in a narrow generated rail clips instead of shrinking — fitting a drawing to its slot is `zoom`'s job (task C). The align overlay's size guard is owed if anyone turns it back on (it ships off). `page.js` took two words outside my fence: `notes:` had to name `sizing`, and one caption said `--panel-hug`.
